sources.title: C-LEO Call 2 Frequently Asked Questions
facts: The FAQ records key dates and application-process clarifications.
Organisations could submit more than one application, subject to quality and completeness requirements.
The FAQ is application guidance, not evidence of awards or operational services.

sources.title: Connectivity in Low Earth Orbit Programme - Call 3
facts: Call 3 opened on 20 July 2026 with a first-stage deadline of 7 September 2026.
Stage-one outcomes were scheduled for 2 October 2026.
The page is a funding opportunity and does not prove future projects will be selected or deployed.

sources.title: UK invests in homegrown space tech to boost national resilience
facts: The government announced more than £62 million for UK space technologies.
The release links space-based services to remote-community broadband and connectivity on rail, in air and at sea.
Funding announcements are investment evidence and not delivery or coverage measurements.

sources.title: UK sets sights on satellite communications market with fresh investment
facts: The government announced £30 million for the second C-LEO funding round.
The programme supports components and technologies for satellite constellations.
The release identifies remote, maritime and aviation connectivity use cases.

sources.title: Satellite communications to improve connectivity in remote areas
facts: Up to £3.5 million was offered for three hybrid-connectivity demonstrators.
Proposed projects included a portable multi-orbit terminal and island demonstrators on Rathlin and Papa Stour.
The projects were trials intended to test hybrid satellite and wireless approaches.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Rural Connectivity Accelerator programme: projects
facts: The RCA programme examines business connectivity needs in rural and very hard-to-reach areas.
Pilots test hybrid broadband, satellite and wireless networks.
The programme focuses on viability, adoption barriers and replicable use cases.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Rural Connectivity Accelerator programme projects - detailed HTML
facts: The Dorset pilot combines aggregated mobile signals with LEO satellite failover for railway and visitor connectivity.
The Ceredigion pilot uses LEO-supported LoRaWAN for environmental monitoring in the River Teifi catchment.
Project descriptions are pilot designs and do not establish production-scale service.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Improving broadband for Very Hard to Reach Premises: Government response
facts: The response analysed demand, benefits, barriers and technology approaches for very hard-to-reach premises.
It received 3,315 responses, including market participants, households and representative organisations.
Satellite, fixed wireless and hybrid technologies were treated as alternatives requiring further evaluation.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Call for Evidence: Improving connectivity for Very Hard to Reach premises
facts: The call estimated that fewer than 100,000 premises might be very hard to reach with gigabit-capable technologies.
It noted limited geographically correlated evidence for non-wired and satellite services.
The consultation sought evidence on demand, benefits, barriers and delivery approaches.

sources.title: ARTES Call for Innovative Hybrid Network Solutions
facts: The call sought expressions of interest for future satellite services supporting the Very Hard to Reach Programme.
It was delivered through ESA's ARTES competitiveness and growth route.
A funding call records intended experimentation rather than operational service.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: UK Wireless Infrastructure Strategy
facts: The strategy describes fixed wireless access as an alternative where fibre deployment is difficult.
It references Alpha Trials testing LEO satellite broadband for very hard-to-reach premises.
Policy commitments and trials must remain distinct from current parcel-level service.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Project Gigabit progress update, December 2023
facts: The update describes the VHTR Alpha Trial programme and Rural Connectivity Accelerator.
It records an £8 million proposed satellite grant fund for up to 35,000 very hard-to-reach premises.
Programme intentions and trial deployment do not establish current orderability.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Digital Inclusion Action Plan: First Steps
facts: The plan sets a cross-government framework for digital inclusion.
It addresses access, skills, confidence and support rather than network coverage alone.
The document is policy evidence and does not provide exact premises connectivity.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Digital Inclusion Action Plan: One Year On
facts: The report reviews one year of delivery following the February 2025 action plan.
It covers first actions, leadership actions and industry pledges.
Progress reporting is programme evidence and not a current coverage dataset.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Digital Inclusion Action Plan: summary of responses
facts: The response summarises evidence submitted after publication of the First Steps plan.
The call for evidence ran from 26 February to 9 April 2025.
Consultation evidence informs policy but is not measured service availability.
